title: Dedicated reserve tiering & value-ladder experiments with enterprise SQ alignment
creator: Maya Patel
description: Investigate and validate a three-tiered reserved GPU packaging model for Dedicated: Flex (small reserve + burst credits), Core (predictable reserve with soft autoscale), and Premium (guaranteed throughput + enhanced SLA and on-call). The goal is to produce a consumer-facing value ladder, contract language aligned with typical enterprise SQ answers, and a 6-week experimentation plan to A/B test messaging, default bands, and burst credit economics with existing pilot customers.
acceptance_criteria: Drafted pricing bands with per-GPU equivalent monthly pricing and burst credit rules for Flex/Core/Premium
Companion contract clause drafts (SLA, preemption, data isolation, KMS) that map to standard SQ items
Experiment plan with control/variant definitions, customer segmentation, and measurement dashboard links
Sales enablement one-pager and internal playbook for negotiation fallback rules
Sign-off from Legal on SQ/contract language and Security on KMS/audit commitments
proposed_packages: Flex: 2-16 vGPU-equivalent reserve bands, up to 2x burst credits pool, no hard SLA, 14-day rolling commitment
Core: 16-128 vGPU-equivalent reserve bands, soft autoscale to +25% with prioritized queueing, 99.9% uptime SLO, 1mo commit
Premium: 128+ vGPU-equivalent reserve bands, guaranteed throughput lanes, dedicated failover region option, 99.95% SLA, enterprise pricing & support
experiment_design: Run three parallel experiments: (A) pricing ladder messaging on the contract quote page vs control messaging; (B) default autoscale cap at 20% vs 40% for Core customers to observe spend/latency outcomes; (C) burst credit top-ups sold as add-on vs included in Flex. Each experiment uses a randomized assignment of new pilot quotes and a set of 12 existing pilot customers for cross-over testing. Measurement window: 30 days post-commit. Rollback criteria: >15% negative impact on ARR conversion or >10% increase in token-unit cost for platform.
success_metrics: Conversion rate on pilot quotes (target +8% relative to baseline)
Net dollar retention uplift for customers migrating to Core/Premium (+5% over 6 months)
Average utilization delta vs reserve band (target 60-85% utilization for Core)
Incidence of SLA breaches (target <1/month aggregate for Premium cohorts)
Sales cycle velocity change (target -10% for customers accepting Flex/Core default terms)

notes: Key trade-offs: aggressive burst inclusion simplifies sales pitch but risks margin erosion; tight autoscale caps protect economics but may reduce sale conversion. Mitigation: burst top-ups as short-term promotional add-on and telemetry to measure evasion patterns. Longer-term: consider conversion credit for customers who switch to higher tiers after sustained usage.
